title: P0 hosted API - intermittent stream fractionation timeline digest
summary: On 2030-02-20 we observed a P0 degradation where ~0.8% of streaming sessions experienced repeated fragment reassembly failures and elevated tail latency (p99) for 27 minutes. Customers saw increased streaming stalls and client reconnects. The incident correlated with a recent change to the edge multiplexing path plus transient ingestion backpressure in telemetry which delayed root-cause detection.
impact:
- Duration: 27 minutes (2030-02-20 16:03–16:30 UTC)
- Affected sessions: ~0.8% of active streaming sessions during window (~12k sessions)
- Symptoms: streaming stalls, repeated small chunk re-transmits, p99 streaming latency increased from 820ms to 6.4s, visible client reconnect spikes and ~0.5% increase in upstream 5xx errors
- Customer-visible: chat/time-to-first-token delays, partial responses requiring client reconnect; two enterprise customers opened support tickets during the window
- Financial/Risk: no SLA breach on availability but degraded customer experience and elevated support overhead
timeline:
- 16:00 UTC: Canary rollout of multiplexing path optimization (edge-proxy v3.14) starts (canary 2%).
- 16:02 UTC: Stream fragment reassembly errors begin to appear in edge logs (low signal, sampled).
- 16:03 UTC: First automated streaming-errors alert (OBS) fires but rate below threshold; paging not triggered.
- 16:06 UTC: Support reports customer reconnects; SRE oncall triages.
- 16:08 UTC: Manual dashboards show sudden p99 spike for streaming; sampling traces show fragmented chunk ordering on some connections.
- 16:10 UTC: SRE increases sampling and turns on verbose edge logs. Telemetry ingest begins to lag due to heavier sampling.
- 16:14 UTC: Hypothesis: new multiplexing path plus Nagle-like aggregation on client TCP causing out-of-order chunk boundaries.
- 16:16 UTC: Rollback of edge-proxy v3.14 to v3.13 initiated for canary hosts.
- 16:20 UTC: Canary rollback shows immediate reduction in fragmentation errors on those hosts.
- 16:23 UTC: Full rollback to v3.13 across edge fleet completed.
- 16:27 UTC: Metrics return to normal; post-incident monitoring kept at elevated sampling.
- 16:30 UTC: Incident declared mitigated.
- 16:45 UTC: Initial incident note drafted and support/customer outreach templated.
detection_and_observability_notes: Detection relied on low-sampling edge logs and downstream user reports; automated alert thresholds were tuned to higher absolute error rates and missed early low-volume signal. Increased sampling helped confirm the hypothesis but caused telemetry ingestion lag which masked some internal signals. Missing telemetry: per-connection fragment boundary telemetry and explicit multiplexing-flag tracing were not emitted at the required cardinality.
root_cause: A logic regression in the new multiplexing optimization introduced a rare condition where sequence boundary markers could be dropped when small writes coincided with the edge host's aggregation timer. This produced fragmented payloads that the reassembly code path did not expect, causing repeated fragment reordering and transient reassembly failures. The issue was only likely when client TCP behavior produced many sub-200B writes and coincided with specific aggregation timers (Nagle-like). The problem surfaced only after the canary rollout and only for a small percentage of sessions. Contributing factor: insufficient high-cardinality tracing for the multiplexing flags and aggressive telemetry sampling thresholds that delayed signal amplification.
immediate_remediation_actions:
- Rolled back edge-proxy v3.14 to v3.13 across the fleet (completed by 16:23 UTC).
- Increased keepalive/connection timers on the edge to reduce interaction with client-side aggregation for the short term.
- Escalated to engineers on multiplexing and reassembly code to produce a targeted fix.
- Increased sampling on observability pipelines to capture per-connection fragment metadata (temporary, careful to avoid ingestion overload).
- Notified support and initiated customer communications for impacted accounts.
permanent_remediation_plan:
- Implement robust sequence boundary markers in multiplexing protocol and defensive checks in reassembly path (PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1193).
- Add unit and fuzz tests that simulate many small writes and aggregation timing edge-cases.
- Revisit aggregation timer heuristics to avoid problematic alignment with client write patterns.
- Ensure multiplexing feature flag defaults to off for marginal networks and add gradual rollout gating by observed fragment error rate.
- Backfill high-cardinality tracing for multiplexing decisions and per-connection fragment metrics.
- Improve telemetry ingestion autoscaling safeguards so temporarily increasing sampling cannot cause blind spots.
short_term_followups:
- Merge and canary the defensive reassembly fix behind a feature flag.
- Create an automated metric: 'fraction_of_streams_with_fragmentation_errors' and alert when >0.2% sustained for 5m.
- Update runbook to include explicit early-page conditions for low-volume but high-impact streaming reassembly errors.
- Run replay test harness for edge-proxy using captured session traces to validate fixes.
- Reach out to the two enterprise customers with detailed timeline and remediation plan.
mitigation_runbook_excerpt:
- If fragment reassembly errors are observed: 1) verify rollouts (is v3.14 active?) 2) if yes, immediately scale canary down and rollback canary hosts; 3) increase edge keepalive to 90s; 4) enable verbose fragment tracing for affected hosts only; 5) if rollback not possible, route affected traffic to dedicated fallback pool with v3.13 until fix is deployed.
- Pager criteria update: page on >0.2% fragment_error_fraction sustained for 3 consecutive minutes or repeated customer support tickets referencing streaming stalls from multiple tenants.
detection_metrics:
- p99 streaming latency (baseline 820ms -> incident 6.4s)
- fragment_error_fraction (sampled) spiked to 1.1% on canary hosts
- client reconnect rate +420% compared to baseline during window
- telemetry ingest lag increased by 18% when sampling was raised
- overall 5xx rate up 0.5 percentage points
lessons_learned:
- Feature rollouts that touch stream reassembly need higher-fidelity tracing and tighter rollout gates.
- Low-signal bugs can still be high impact; alerting must account for relative tail metrics, not only absolute counts.
- Telemetry instrumentation changes during incidents can introduce new blind spots; rely on reserved low-volume debug sinks for safe expansion.
- Runbook should include immediate steps for sampling increases (ingest safety limits) and a checklist for rolling back complex networking changes.
communication_notes:
- Initial customer-facing message sent to affected customers within 90 minutes.
- Internal incident bridge maintained during mitigation; SRE and Edge team coordinated the rollback.
- Post-incident postmortem to be scheduled with product, SRE, edge, and support for 48 hours after mitigation.
- Suggested public postmortem draft to product comms after internal review.
